title: Novelty vs. Effectiveness: A Campus Lecture on Choosing What Works
instructions: 本材料为模拟教育内容，非官方雅思试题，也不代表任何官方分数。请先听录音（或阅读文字稿），完成10道听力/阅读题；然后学习语法讲解并完成8道语法题；最后完成口语与写作任务。听力部分注意不同说话者的语气和自然修正。所有题目答案必须来自材料原文。
transcript:
Professor Lin: Good morning, everyone. Today I want to talk about a question that comes up in every field: is the newest idea always the best one? Let me start with a small story. Last year, a student group at our university built a very fancy app for finding study partners. It had bright colors, funny sounds, and a robot helper. Everyone loved it for two weeks. Then people stopped using it. Why? Because it did not help students actually meet. The app was novel, but it was not effective.

Student A (Mia): Professor, sorry to interrupt. So you are saying novelty is bad?

Professor Lin: No, not at all. Novelty is not bad. It is just not the same as effectiveness. Novelty means something feels new and different. Effectiveness means something actually works and produces results. A new method can be exciting, but if it does not solve the problem, it is only entertainment.

Student B (David): But sometimes a new method is the only way to get better results. For example, online classes were new for many teachers, and now they are normal.

Professor Lin: That is a fair point, David. However, online classes became useful only after teachers changed how they taught. The technology was new, but the effectiveness came from better planning. So novelty can open a door, but it does not walk through the door for you.

Student C (Sophie): I think I disagree a little. If people are bored, they will not try anything. A new idea can make people interested. Isn't interest important?

Professor Lin: Yes, interest matters. But interest is a starting point, not a finish line. Let me give you another example. A hospital tried a new system for organizing medicine. It looked modern and everyone was excited. After three months, nurses made more mistakes, not fewer. The system was new, but it was not effective. The hospital then went back to an older system, with small changes. The older system was not exciting, but it was safer.

Student A: So the old system was better because it worked?

Professor Lin: Exactly. The old system was more effective. It was less novel, but it was more useful. This is the key difference. We often confuse "new" with "better." But new and better are two different questions. Ask first: Does it work? Then ask: Is it new?

Student B: What about when a new idea is both new and effective?

Professor Lin: That is the best case. But it is rare. Most new ideas need time and testing. A new idea is a hypothesis, not a result. You must test it. If it works, keep it. If it does not work, change it or drop it. Do not keep a bad idea just because it is new.

Student C: But some people say we should always try new things. Is that wrong?

Professor Lin: Trying new things is good, but trying is not the same as keeping. You can try a new idea and still decide it is not effective. That is not failure. That is learning. The danger is when we love novelty so much that we forget to ask about results.

Student A: So how do we decide?

Professor Lin: Use a simple test. First, define the problem clearly. Second, try the new idea on a small scale. Third, measure the results. Fourth, compare with the old way. If the new way is better, use it. If not, do not use it just because it is new. This test is not exciting, but it is effective.

Student B: That sounds slow.

Professor Lin: It can be slow. But slow and careful is often better than fast and wrong. Remember: novelty gets attention. Effectiveness gets results. We need both, but we need effectiveness more. Thank you. We will continue next week.

questions.prompt: What was the main problem with the student group's app?
options: It did not help students actually meet.
It was too expensive to build.

questions.prompt: According to Professor Lin, what does novelty mean?
questions.explanation: 教授给出定义：novelty 指某物感觉新且不同。

questions.prompt: What happened after the hospital used the new medicine system for three months?
options: Nurses made more mistakes, not fewer.
answers: Nurses made more mistakes, not fewer.
questions.explanation: 原文说三个月后护士犯更多错误，而不是更少。

questions.prompt: What did the hospital do after the new system failed?
options: It went back to an older system with small changes.
answers: It went back to an older system with small changes.

questions.evidence: The hospital then went back to an older system, with small changes.

questions.explanation: 教授说新想法是假设，必须测试。

options: That is a waste of time.

questions.explanation: 原文结尾对比：新颖获得关注，有效获得结果。

questions.explanation: 教授说两者都需要，但更需要有效性。

grammar.title: 转折、让步、同意与不同意；转述观点
grammar.explanation: 在英语中，表达不同观点时常用转折词（but, however, although）和让步结构（even though, while it is true that...）。同意可以说 I agree / That is a fair point；不同意可以说 I disagree / I see your point, but...。转述他人观点时常用动词如 say, argue, point out, suggest，并注意时态后移（如 "I think" 转述为 "He said he thought"）。注意：although 和 but 不能同时用于同一句；however 是副词，需用逗号隔开。
grammar.example: That is a fair point, David. However, online classes became useful only after teachers changed how they taught.

options: Although the app was new, it was not effective.
Although the app was new, but it was not effective.
The app was new, although it was not effective, but.
Although the app was new, however it was not effective.
answers: Although the app was new, it was not effective.
questions.explanation: although 引导让步状语从句，主句前不再用 but 或 however。
questions.evidence: Although the app was new, it was not effective.

options: The system was modern. However, nurses made more mistakes.
The system was modern, however nurses made more mistakes.
The system was modern however, nurses made more mistakes.
However the system was modern, nurses made more mistakes.
answers: The system was modern. However, nurses made more mistakes.
questions.explanation: however 是副词，连接两个句子时前面用句号，后面用逗号。
questions.evidence: The system was modern. However, nurses made more mistakes.

questions.prompt: Choose the best way to disagree politely.
options: I see your point, but I think interest is not enough.
I disagree completely and I will not listen.
answers: I see your point, but I think interest is not enough.
questions.explanation: 礼貌不同意先承认对方观点，再用 but 引出自己的看法。
questions.evidence: I see your point, but I think interest is not enough.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct reported speech: Mia said, "I think novelty is not bad."
options: Mia said she thought novelty was not bad.
Mia said she thinks novelty is not bad.
Mia said I think novelty is not bad.
Mia says she thought novelty was not bad.
answers: Mia said she thought novelty was not bad.
questions.explanation: 转述过去说话，时态后移：think→thought, is→was，人称 I→she。
questions.evidence: Mia said she thought novelty was not bad.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence with 'while it is true that'.
options: While it is true that novelty attracts attention, effectiveness matters more.
While it is true that novelty attracts attention, but effectiveness matters more.
While it is true that novelty attracts attention, however effectiveness matters more.
While it is true that novelty attracts attention, effectiveness matters more, although.
answers: While it is true that novelty attracts attention, effectiveness matters more.
questions.explanation: while it is true that 引导让步，主句不再用 but 或 however。
questions.evidence: While it is true that novelty attracts attention, effectiveness matters more.

options: Even though the old system was not exciting, it was safer.
Even though the old system was not exciting, but it was safer.
Even though the old system was not exciting, however it was safer.
Even though the old system was not exciting, it was safer, but.
answers: Even though the old system was not exciting, it was safer.
questions.explanation: even though 引导让步，主句不用 but 或 however。
questions.evidence: Even though the old system was not exciting, it was safer.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct reported speech: David said, "Online classes are normal now."
options: David said online classes were normal then.
David said online classes are normal now.
David says online classes were normal then.
David said online classes were normal now.
answers: David said online classes were normal then.
questions.explanation: 转述过去说话，时态后移 are→were，now→then。
questions.evidence: David said online classes were normal then.

questions.prompt: Choose the best way to agree with a point.
questions.explanation: That is a fair point 是表示同意对方观点的常用表达。
